formal_specification.domain: Any public recipe type K satisfying the declared lawful exact field/root protocol. Nontrivial fixed recipes additionally require their exact roots/sqrt2/phi. Typed refusals are part of the API.

invariant_argument: Admission/size: AbelianGroup::new checks each factor>=2, checked product<=32 and copies factors only after acceptance. Thus a public admitted list has at most5 factors and each factor<=32, including the empty list with unit group of order1. Square exponent admission precedes private PhasePlan indexing; group.digits produces exactly that many digits, each below its matching factor.

Signed exactness: let g=gcd(m_i,m_j)>0 and r=b_ij rem_euclid g, so0<=r<g for every i64, including MIN/MAX. c=gcd(r,g)>0, numerator=r/c and denominator=g/c are reduced, denominator divides both factors, and r=0 gives(0,1). These usize casts/divisions therefore neither narrow a large signed input nor divide by zero.

Root order: every reduced denominator divides a factor and hence product(moduli). Inductively its lcm L also divides that positive product, so1<=L<=32. The lcm update (L/gcd(L,d))*d is the exact lcm, with intermediate/result<=32. Each weight numerator*(L/d)<L. Roots are powers of one admitted generator of this actual order, not an unnecessarily large nominal conductor.

Mixed-radix transport: d_ij divides both m_i,m_j. For w_ij=a_ij*(L/d_ij), both w_ij*m_i and w_ij*m_j are integer multiples of L. Replacing digits by their group-coordinate residues therefore leaves sum w_ij*x_i*y_j modulo L unchanged. Bilinearity descends to the actual product of cyclic groups; it is not merely bilinearity on a single common ZMod carrier. Basis-coordinate pairs isolate individual coefficient phases, so their reduced orders generate exactly the lcm subgroup.

Phase safety: at most25 summands have w,x,y<32, hence each<32768 and the sum<=819175<2^20, within 32/64-bit usize. L stays positive, so modulo and roots[index] are safe. Matching vector lengths are private caller preconditions established at the only production call, not an admission claim for arbitrary malformed private fixtures.

Law composition: ribbon calls FusionCategory::new then BraidedFusionCategory::new then RibbonFusionCategory::try_new. The first two establish symbol layout/invertibility and commutative R support; try_new calls braided.validate, which calls category.validate and both direct/mirror hexagon scans, then checks dimensions, unit/nonzero/dual-invariant twists and ribbon monodromy. Successful public recipe output has passed these provider checks, not just record allocation.

Named recipes: Ising uses dimensions(1,sqrt2,1), F_sigma=[1,1;1,-1]/sqrt2, its stated off-block signs and the listed16th-root R phases. Fibonacci uses dimensions(1,phi), fixed gauge F=[phi-1,1;phi-1,1-phi] and10th-root phases; (phi-1)^2+(phi-1)=1 ensures that block squares to I. This gauge is not advertised as orthonormal. Semion uses the -1 associator and i phase. Toric/three-fermion/double/cyclic wrappers select exactly the recorded bicharacter/labels; recipe names do not prove a classification or Drinfeld-center equivalence.

Ownership/cost: the phase plan uses O(r^2 log32) integer work and O(r^2) weights, caching exactlyL roots and n digit vectors in O(L+nr) storage. R lookup uses O(r^2) small-integer work and one necessary owned field clone per admitted R entry. Powers do not allocate intermediate field vectors per pair; the final unused root multiplication is absent. Two coefficient passes avoid an extra reduced-coefficient table. Fixed F/R helper closures clone only coefficients required for owned output entries.

Provider cost boundary: ring construction/validation, sparse F/R storage, exact block inversions, pentagon/hexagon traversal and dimension/ribbon validation remain their actual content-pinned provider algorithms and default admissions. The category provider preflights logical storage and label/law work using DEFAULT_CATEGORY_LIMITS(2^20 elements,2^28 scalar-work units); rank and multiplicity-free bounds keep its widened counts safe. This review does not replace those costs with a misleading O(r^2) total or promise every rank32 recipe fits every field/resource policy.

trust_boundary: Lawful immutable characteristic-zero exact field values, rational embedding, compatible conjugation and root generators; honest optional rational/sign projections. FusionScalar is an open protocol and cannot enforce those laws for arbitrary client implementations. Rust/compiler, pinned thiserror and exact matrix/ring/category/ribbon/scalar providers are explicit dependencies. Logical element/operation counts exclude scalar bit length, comparison/clone cost, allocator metadata and OS memory. No arbitrary client panic or allocator-totality theorem is asserted.
consumer_review: lib.rs and mod.rs export the same catalog source; the repository root re-exports the local tfqm package, whose Cargo manifest binds actual external number-theory/matrix path dependencies. No consumer inherits a completed grade.

The two local tests in braided.rs use Ising materialization; current canonical both-root suites compile those exact callers. The catalog fixture directly exercises all public recipe wrappers, signed extremes, missing fields, shape priority and an empty group.

All final constructors call the actual provider chain reviewed above; a law-invalid fixed recipe cannot bypass pentagon/hexagon/dimension/ribbon admission. Generic custom field/root choices may validly refuse. No public API promises every field or pointed braiding is nondegenerate.

Catalog does not call this producer. ModularData callers in the preserved SU2 tests are unchanged and replay all supported levels against the current implementation in both actual roots. Old catalog/modular mutation receipts remain old executions; this bridge establishes their unchanged consumer boundary and current composition, not a new mutation replay or general Rust refinement.
assurance_limits: AuthorityEffect: None. These are bounded exact construction/checking/computation APIs; no physical authority, publication or whole-workspace verification is inferred.
